summary: The audit checks 45 units, all numbered 100 or higher and at least half in graduate courses. In the Music, Science, and Technology subplan it also checks MUSIC 201, 220A, 251, 256A and 320 and 6 units of capstone work in MUSIC 220C, 220D or 298 spread over at least two enrollments, each with an A or B grade (or an S in a course offered only credit/no credit). Checked by hand: three CCRMA electives you move in, A, B or S grades in your other Music courses, that the capstone units fall in at least two quarters, no course shared with your BA, and, in the other subplans (for doctoral students adding the MA), the qualifying exams and advancement to candidacy.

MWLIRGTU.why: "All of the following fields of study are declarable as subplans in Axess": a list of the subplans, not a requirement.

sUtO9KX5.why: "A minimum of 45 academic units is required for a master's degree in music" is program.unitsMin; "At least half of those units must be in courses with the career GR code" is program.gradUnitsShare; "all must be at the 100-level or higher" is a program total. What stays a hand check: "Only work that receives a grade of A, B, or S (a passing grade in an instructor-mandated credit/no credit course) in Music courses numbered 100 or higher taken as a graduate student is recognized", a grade rule for Music courses only (the MST course rules apply it), and the rule that BA courses do not count twice.
